newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa donates police equipment to former Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa donates police equipment to former Zaire.

text.p: South Africa said on Thursday it was donating police equipment worth 1.5 millon rand ($330,000) to the new Democratic Republic of the Congo, formerly Zaire.
The donation includes tearsmoke grenades, targas masks, handcuffs, boots, megaphones and radios, policing minister Sydney Mufamadi said in a statement.
Uniforms which belonged to South Africa's police forces under the old apartheid regime also formed part of the consignment, he added.

"The government agreed to make this donation because we believe it will contribute to the process of rebuilding the Democratic Republic of the Congo and put it on the road to stability and prosperity," Mufamadi said.
He confirmed he met the new Congo's Minister of the Interior, Mwenzi Kongolo, earlier this week to discuss assistance and said the request for police equipment was made at these talks.

Earlier on Thursday, South Africa called for an Africa-led international effort to help rebuild the shattered economy of Laurent Kabila's government in the Congo, following last month's overthrow of president Mobutu Sese Seko's government.

Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad, fresh from a two-day visit to Kinshasa, said Kabila aimed to target infrastructure development, reforms at the central bank, the launch of a new currency and the promotion of industrialisation -- mainly in manufacturing and mining.
